title: Regular sequences and the canonical completed quotient presentation
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be a finitely generated ideal, and put $B=R/I$. Let $\widehat R$ be the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $R$ and let $\widehat B$ be the completion of $B$ at its maximal ideal. The canonical surjection $q:\widehat R\to\widehat B$ has the property that $I$ is generated by a finite $R$-regular sequence contained in $\mathfrak m$ if and only if $\ker q$ is generated by a finite $\widehat R$-regular sequence contained in the maximal ideal of $\widehat R$.

source.place: Tags 00MA (completion tensor), 00MB (completion flat), and 09Q1 setup; regularity of the completed local ring via More on Algebra Tag 07NY.

proof.text: Put $S=\widehat R$, with canonical map $c:R\to S$, and put $J=IS$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $S$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mS$ and residue field $k=R/\mathfrak m$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], $B$ has maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$, and its powers are the images of $\mathfrak m^n$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient], applied to $R\to R/I$, gives the canonical map $q$, its surjectivity and $\ker q=J$. Completing $0\to I\to R\to B\to0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] identifies the completion $I^\wedge$ of the $R$-module $I$ with $J$ as an $S$-module: the completed inclusion is injective with image $\ker q$. These are the coordinatewise maps, so $a\in I$ maps to $c(a)\in J$.

source.place: Tags 05GI, 05GG, 0316, 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor) and 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), applied to the finite module exact sequence for R/I.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] to the ideal $\mathfrak m$ and module $I$, with exponent $1$. Together with the $S$-linear identification $I^\wedge=J$ of step 1, it gives $I/\mathfrak m I\cong J/\mathfrak nJ$ as $k$-vector spaces, carrying the class of $a$ to that of $c(a)$. Indeed $\mathfrak m I^\wedge$ maps to $\mathfrak mJ=\mathfrak nJ$: expand every element of $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mS$ as a finite sum $\sum c(a_j)s_j$ and absorb $s_j$ into the factor in $J$. The identification respects $k$ by the residue-field map in step 1.

For the forward implication, let $f_1,\ldots,f_t\in I$ be a regular generating sequence. For $0\leq i<t$, put $P_i=(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$ and $M_i=R/P_i$. Multiplication $\mu_i$ by $f_{i+1}$ on $M_i$ is injective by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and its cokernel is $M_{i+1}$. Complete the exact sequence $0\to M_i\xrightarrow{\mu_i}M_i\to M_{i+1}\to0$ using [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules]. The resulting multiplication map is injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient], $M_i^\wedge=S/P_iS$; this isomorphism sends each compatible residue class to the same class in the quotient, so the completed map is multiplication by $c(f_{i+1})$. The final quotient $S/IS$ is nonzero because $IS\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Therefore $c(f_1),\ldots,c(f_t)$ is regular and generates $J=\ker q$.

source.place: Tags 00LF (definition-regular-sequence), 00MA and 00MB, applied successively to the prefix quotients.

proof.text: For the reverse implication, suppose $y_1,\ldots,y_r\in\mathfrak n$ is a regular generating sequence of $J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free], $J/J^2$ has the displayed basis $y_j\bmod J^2$ over $S/J$. Since $J\subseteq\mathfrak n$, we have $J^2\subseteq\mathfrak nJ$, and quotienting this basis isomorphism by $\mathfrak n/J$ gives a basis $y_j\bmod\mathfrak nJ$ of $J/\mathfrak nJ$ over $k$: componentwise reduction of $(S/J)^r$ is $k^r$. In particular this vector space has dimension $r$.

source.place: Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), degree 1, followed by componentwise quotient of a finite free module.

proof.text: Using step 2, choose a basis of $I/\mathfrak mI$ of length $r$ and lift its entries to $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], these generate $I$, since $I$ is finitely generated. Their images $z_j=c(f_j)$ then generate $J=IS$: expand any element of $I$ in the $f_j$ and extend its coefficients to $S$. Now $J$ is a finite $S$-module with the two generating $r$-tuples $y$ and $z$, so [lem-pur-local-generating-tuples] gives $P=(p_{jk})\in\mathrm{GL}_r(S)$ with $z_j=\sum_kp_{jk}y_k$. Put $C=S/J$. By [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial], $\theta_y:C[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\operatorname{gr}_J(S)$, $T_k\mapsto[y_k]_1$, is an isomorphism. Let $\sigma$ be the $C$-algebra endomorphism $T_j\mapsto\sum_k\bar p_{jk}T_k$; it is a graded automorphism, with inverse given by the image of $P^{-1}$. Since $[z_j]_1=\sum_k\bar p_{jk}[y_k]_1$, the map $\theta_z:T_j\mapsto[z_j]_1$ equals $\theta_y\circ\sigma$, hence is an isomorphism. As $S$ is Noetherian local (step 1), $z_j\in J\subseteq\mathfrak n$ and $J=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$, [lem-pur-quasi-regular-noetherian-local] shows that $c(f_1),\ldots,c(f_r)$ is regular in $S$. For $r=0$ all tuples are empty and $J=0$; the same citations apply.

source.place: Algebra Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK) for the lifted generators; More on Algebra Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), part (1) and its proof, with Algebra 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular) and 061S (lemma-quasi-regular-regular) in algebra.tex.

proof.text: Fix $0\leq i<r$, put $P_i=(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$, $M_i=R/P_i$, and let $K_i$ and $L_i$ be the kernel and image of multiplication $\mu_i=f_{i+1}$ on $M_i$. These are finite $R$-modules by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], since $M_i$ is cyclic. Complete $0\to K_i\to M_i\to L_i\to0$ and $0\to L_i\to M_i\to M_i/L_i\to0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules]. The first gives $K_i^\wedge$ as the kernel of $M_i^\wedge\to L_i^\wedge$; the second makes $L_i^\wedge\to M_i^\wedge$ injective. Their composite is $\mu_i^\wedge$, by its coordinatewise formula. Under [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient], $M_i^\wedge=S/P_iS$ and this composite multiplies by $c(f_{i+1})$, which is injective by step 5. Hence $K_i^\wedge=0$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] gives $K_i/\mathfrak mK_i=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] with submodule $0\subseteq K_i$: it yields $K_i=0$. This proves every required multiplication on $R/P_i$ injective. Finally $R/I\neq0$ since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] proves $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ regular.

source.place: Tags 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), 00MB, 00MA, 05GG, 00DV and 00LF; exactness and Nakayama reflect injectivity of each multiplication map.

proof.text: The forward implication and the reverse implication give the claimed equivalence, using $\ker q=IS$ from step 1. If $I=0$, the forward construction uses the empty sequence. Conversely, a regular sequence generating $J=0$ must have length $0$ by the conormal basis in step 4, and steps 2 and 5 give $I=0$ by Nakayama. Thus the empty-sequence case is included.

lean.statement: theorem completionRegularKernelPreservation {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (hIfg : I.FG) : let B := R ⧸ I let m := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R let n := Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) m let c := AdicCompletion.exists_local_completion_quotient R B (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective) let q : AdicCompletion m R →+* AdicCompletion n B := c.2.choose Function.Surjective q ∧ ((∃ xs : List R, RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R xs ∧ Ideal.ofList xs = I ∧ ∀ x ∈ xs, x ∈ m) ↔ (∃ ys : List (AdicCompletion m R), RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (AdicCompletion m R) ys ∧ Ideal.ofList ys = RingHom.ker q ∧ ∀ y ∈ ys, y ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (AdicCompletion m R)))
lean.note: The completion ideal n is the image of the maximal ideal of R under R → R ⧸ I; under hI this is the maximal ideal of B. The chosen q is the canonical coordinatewise completion map supplied by AdicCompletion.exists_local_completion_quotient, whose witness includes surjectivity and kernel identification.
